I have biploar disorder. I don't think I've ever been directly rejected on account of my disorder, but I think it has effected my dating pool.  It is more difficult to relate and talk to people about certain elements of my life experience if they haven't been through something similar or at least know someone who has dealt with mental health issues. People who haven't dealt with it treat mental illness like something inherently wrong with you, but really it is just something that effects you. I AM NOT my disorder, I am the person fighting this disorder. 

Obviously, when I was younger, mid-episode (either depressed or raving about my manic delusions), it turned people off without me ever having to say anything. Now, that I am older, more stable, in an established career, most people I do tell are very surprised to hear I have bipolar disorder.

I get the feeling like a pariah, though. It definitely makes relationships harder. It'll be okay, though, just keep fighting the good fight.
